title: Qt: I/O Graph support of Average Over Time interpretation
description:
Introduce a new interpretation then raw indicators such as
Packets, Bytes, and Bits, have an Average Over Time interpretation.

Respectively, this brings Packets/s, Bytes/s, and Bits/s,
providing throughput like indicators.

Fix #19975

Quick notes for the reviewer:
- the suggested implementation enables/disables the _avg over time_ checkbox following any change of the _Y Axis_ value. If a previous value of this _Y Axis_ was set to Packets/Bytes/Bits and the checkbox was checked, it will stay checked and not accepting any change until the _Y Axis_ is set back to Packets/Bytes/Bits. Clicking on the _avg over time_ column results with a line selection.
- As the number of UATs for the I/O Graph is increased by one, on the first opening of that window the user will get a warning pop-up, this is expected and the second window opening will work and load the defaults settings.

![expected_notif](/uploads/38371f96b14ce9d948d7052e1ba876d8/expected_notif.JPG)

I don't think it's a good idea to remove the users I/O Graphs when upgrading Wireshark, this will give frustrated users. Putting this in the end would be the way to go.

Also, the new column header is using only lowercase while all others start with uppercase.
A benefactor took care of your remarks.

There is a problem with this change- by inserting a new column in the middle of the UAT configuration file for I/O Graphs, the files are not backwards compatible with 4.2 and 4.4. It would be better to add the new column at the end, so that it could be set to default if missing and would be ignored by earlier versions if present.

Restarting Wireshark isn't enough ? I've noted above that the first run is not good. Does it mean you used switched back to an elder version after running the "new" I/O graph ?

It doesn't seem very intuitive to me to always add new columns at the end. That's not really the subject here, but that's not cool.

Yes, I mean if you switch back and forth. It's not unusual for people to do that for various reasons.

We don't necessarily have to display the columns in the GUI in the same order (though that requires some work on the Qt model code) as the file, but for the file format as stored it's useful. The format is basically a CSV format, and doesn't have headers.

No headers indeed, and also no versioning, that worked well for a long time. I will look at it but I believe that at least 99% of users just upgrade when a new version is available and never go back to an older version (the list of bugs fixed always being very convincing).

See !18120 for how you do it. Add the new entry to the end, provide a default value, and them call `header()->moveSection()` after setting the model so that the default visual index changes (the user can still move the columns) without changing the ordering in the model.

That makes it backwards and forwards compatible.
I'm building a new dev platform because of Qt6, be right back
OKay I have seen what you did, thanks for this.

@@ -422,6 +422,11 @@ Individual graphs can be configured using the following options:
 Enabled::
 Draw or don’t draw this graph.
 
+avg over time::
+When checked and the “Y Axis” value is one of Packets/Bytes/Bits, the displayed value is an average over time
+based on the _Interval_, instead of the raw value. The ordinary throughput is obtained when “Y Axis” is set
+to _Bits_.
+
 Graph Name::
 The name of this graph.
